items.title: Custom export options get serialized even when you specify not to
items.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.stable, 4.5.stable

I haven't tested on more versions but I guess it also happens.

### System information

Godot v4.5.stable (8fe6f198d) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1047) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600G with Radeon Graphics (12 threads) - 31.89 GiB memory

### Issue description

When creating plugins to export for other platforms, when adding the export options for other platforms we can do something like:

```cpp
r_options->push_back(ExportOption(PropertyInfo(Variant::CALLABLE, "application/generate_metadata", PROPERTY_HINT_TOOL_BUTTON, "Generate Metadata", PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR), Callable(this, "generate_metadata")));
```

This creates a button and calls the generate_metadata function when clicking it, but after saving, the property gets serialized and the Callable instance gets lost.

In this case I haven't specified the PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE flag, which according to the documentation is the one that enables the serialization, therefore in this case the application/generate_metadata shouldn't even get serialized and stored.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the export_plugin.cpp file for any platform
2. Add the following line inside the get_export_options() method:
  ```cpp
  r_options->push_back(ExportOption(PropertyInfo(Variant::CALLABLE, "asdfasdf/generate_metadata", PROPERTY_HINT_TOOL_BUTTON, "Generate Metadata", PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR), Callable()));
  ```
3. Compile and open Godot
4. Generate the export options for the platform you modified and save them
5. On the export options file you should see a line like so:
  ```
  asdfasdf/generate_metadata=Callable()
  ```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

This file is the export_plugin for windows on the commit with tag 4.7-stable, unzip and move this file to: platform/windows/export/export_plugin.cpp:
[export_plugin.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29442395/export_plugin.zip)

After compiling you'll be able to reproduce the issue described.

- Build scripts

- Saving without reopening the scene or project removes the data from file

- Saving doesn't remove data

1. Building the C# code before opening the project

items.title: 4.7 Metal driver crashes
items.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.stable.mono.official [5b4e0cb0f]
- Not reproducible in: v4.6.2.stable.mono (same project, same save)


### System information

Godot v4.7.stable.mono - macOS Tahoe (26.5.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Apple M2 Pro - Apple M2 Pro (12 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono), 

### Issue description

On the native Metal driver (Forward+) in 4.7, a 2D project misrenders and/or crashes. The Vulkan/MoltenVK driver is a 100% reliable workaround — same project, same scene, same save — and 4.6.2 is unaffected. No errors, warnings, or shader-compile failures are logged in any failure mode.

Two distinct symptoms on the Metal driver, depending on scene content:

1. Static CanvasItems fail to render; dynamic ones render fine.
With a populated 2D scene loaded, items whose transform/visual is re-submitted every frame (moving characters, animals, animated UI values) render correctly, while static items (buildings, TileMapLayers, static Labels) silently disappear. The split is purely static-vs-dynamic — items that vanish and items that survive can be the same node type with the same default material, same parent, same z-index (e.g. a building's floor and its walls are both plain Sprite2Ds, yet both vanish while a survivor walking past renders). This is not a material, shader, z-index, theme, or Y-sort issue — the only discriminator is whether the item is re-recorded each frame.

Clearing .godot/shader_cache (which had been populated under the Vulkan driver) changes the symptom — from most static draws missing to some static draws missing — but does not fix it. A symptom that shifts with cache state, with no project-side property distinguishing rendered from dropped items, points squarely at driver-internal state.

2. Hard crash (EXC_BAD_ACCESS / SIGBUS) when many per-instance ShaderMaterials are present.
The real scene applies a trivial canvas_item shadow shader to hundreds of entities via resource_local_to_scene = true materl this crashes ~50 ms after sceneload, inside the renderer, with no GDScript error:

```
Exception Type:  EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGBUS)
Exception Subtype: KERN_PROTECTION_FAILURE at 0x00000001205f0008
VM Region Info: 0x1205f0008 is not in any region. GAP OF 0x16c000 BYTES

Thread 0 Crashed:: com.apple.main-thread
0   libsystem_platform.dylib   _platform_memmove + 424
1-9  Godot (core + rendering server)
10-21 Godot  (mutually-recursive pair 0x1055acf14 ⇄ 0x1074c5ba4 — canvas-item render traversal)
24  CoreFoundation  __CFRUNLOOP_IS_CALLING_OUT_TO_AN_OBSERVER_CALLBACK_FUNCTION__
36  Godot  main + 952
```

Note: I tried to reproduce the crash in isolation and could not — a single shadow material, and even500 unique shadow ShaderMaterials with per-frame uniform updates, render fine on Metal in a minimal scene. So the crash is not the shader itself; it requires the full scene (static geometry + hundredsof local materials + Y-sorted depth), which is the same context where symptom #1 occurs. The two arelikely the same underlying buffer-handling fault at different severities (a dropped draw vs. amemmove past the end of a reused buffer).

### Steps to reproduce

1. On an Apple Silicon Mac, run a populated Forward+ 2D scene (static buildings + TileMapLayers + moving characters) on the Metal driver in 4.7.

items.body:
### Tested versions

4.7-stable

### System information

NixOS

### Issue description

When building Godot 4.7 with system HarfBuzz, the build requires explicit linkage to `hb-raster` symbols, but the build configuration only requests `harfbuzz` and `harfbuzz-icu` via pkg-config. In packaging environments with strict dependency/linking behavior, this leads to link failures unless `-lharfbuzz-raster` is added manually.

In `nixpkgs`, this currently requires a workaround:
```export NIX_LDFLAGS="$NIX_LDFLAGS -lharfbuzz-raster"```

The expectation is that Godot build scripts should request/link the required HarfBuzz raster component directly when raster APIs are used.

Related NixOS PR: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/533148

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build Godot 4.7 with: `builtin_harfbuzz=false` and LTO enabled (or in strict packaging environments)

items.body:
### Tested versions

In 4.6.3, texture copy had this API:
> Copies the `from_texture` to `to_texture` with the specified `from_pos`, `to_pos` and `size` coordinates. The Z axis of the `from_pos`, `to_pos` and `size` must be `0` for 2-dimensional textures.

In 4.7, the api has changed (and causes errors to print):
> Copies the `from_texture` to `to_texture` with the specified `from_pos`, `to_pos` and `size` coordinates. For 2-dimensional textures, `from_pos` and `to_pos` must have a Z axis of `0`, and `size` must have a Z axis of `1`.

This commit made the change:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/e7519d48492ddc94bd1fa63d3b0dfa4d23422ae9

N/A

This change was not documented here:
https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html

The documentation on the method was updated, but this is a breaking API change and is not listed in the common places.

items.title: Image format RGB8 not supported by hardware, converting to RGBA8
items.body:
### Tested versions

This error does not occur in Godot 4.4.1 or earlier. The bug appears in Godot 4.5 and above, and it is also present up to the stable 4.7 release.

### System information

Arch Linux, Processor: Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-8750H, Dedicated GPU: GeForce GTX 1050 Ti, Proprietary Nvidia driver, working correctly and running many games flawlessly, version: 580.159.04

### Issue description

**The bug that occurs is:**

```
WARNING: Image format RGB8 not supported by hardware, converting to RGBA8.
     at: _validate_texture_format (servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/texture_storage.cpp:2829)

W 0:00:04:588   _validate_texture_format: Image format RGB8 not supported by hardware, converting to RGBA8.
  <Fonte em C++>servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/texture_storage.cpp:2829 @ _validate_texture_format()

```

I use a system that captures a screenshot, pixelates it, and then depixelates it – it's my screen transition system. I should have reported this bug since version 4.5, but since version 4.4.1 was serving me well, I put off reporting it and stayed on 4.4.1. I recently decided to upgrade to version 4.6.3, and the bug persists. I also tested it on the stable 4.7 release, and the bug is still there. Note that this bug occurs on both X11 and Wayland, regardless of the WM or DE used, whether it's KDE, Gnome, Sway, Awesome, Openbox, Hyprland, etc.

**The function that takes a screenshot:**

```gdscript
func screenshoot_for_set_texture(_texture) -> void:
	# Captures screenshot and converts to texture with specific format (RGBAFloat)
	
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw  # Wait for next rendered frame
	var capture = get_viewport().get_texture().get_image()  # Capture viewport image
	
	# https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_image.html
	# Convert image to RGBAFloat format (FORMAT_RGBAF)
	capture.convert(Image.FORMAT_RGBAF)  # Convert to float format (more color precision)
	
	var texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(capture)  # Create texture from image
	#print("New format is: ", texture.get_format()) # Should now return 11 (FORMAT_RGBAF)
	
	_texture.texture = texture  # Apply texture to parameter
```

**The screen transition code, which pixelates and then depixelates:**

```gdscript
extends CanvasLayer

@onready var texture_rect: TextureRect = $TextureRect
@onready var player = get_parent().find_child("player")
@onready var anim: AnimationPlayer = $anim

func _ready() -> void:
	Global.level_start = false
	if player.has_method("lock_player"):
		player.lock_player(1.5)
		
	show_new_scene()
	return
	
func change_scene(_level) -> void:
	Global.screenshoot_for_set_texture(texture_rect)
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	visible = true
	anim.play("pixelate")
	await anim.animation_finished
	#get_tree().change_scene_to_file(_level)
	f_load_scene_loading(_level)
	return
	

func show_new_scene() -> bool:
	screenshoot_for_set_texture(texture_rect)
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	anim.play("pixelate_2")
	await anim.animation_finished
	Global.level_start = true
	visible = false
	return false

func f_load_scene_loading(_scene_name) -> void:
	var loading_scene = preload("res://scenes/singletons/loading.tscn").instantiate()
	loading_scene.scene_name = _scene_name
	get_tree().root.add_child(loading_scene)
```

**And the shader that performs the pixelation and depixelation:**

```glsl
shader_type canvas_item;

uniform float pixelFactor: hint_range(0.0, 1.0) = 0.5;

void fragment() {
	vec2 pixelNumber = vec2(textureSize(TEXTURE, 0)) * pixelFactor;
	vec2 pixelatedUV = round(UV * pixelNumber) / pixelNumber;
	COLOR = texture(TEXTURE, pixelatedUV);
}
```

---

### Steps to reproduce

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Set up a screen transition system that captures a screenshot using `get_viewport().get_texture().get_image()`.
2. Convert the captured image to `Image.FORMAT_RGBAF` using `capture.convert(Image.FORMAT_RGBAF)`.
3. Create an `ImageTexture` from the converted image and assign it to a `TextureRect`.
4. Apply a shader that pixelates the texture using a `pixelFactor` uniform (rounding UV coordinates).
5. Run the transition on both X11 and Wayland, under any WM/DE (KDE, Gnome, Sway, etc.).
6. Observe the warning: `WARNING: Image format RGB8 not supported by hardware, converting to RGBA8.` even though the image was explicitly converted to `FORMAT_RGBAF`.

In this test project, I tested directly on version 4.7, and on 4.7 the following 

```

```

items.title: DynamicFont: Mixing CJK characters with brackets causes excessive DrawCalls due to font atlas pagination
items.body:
### Tested versions

## Issue Description

When using DynamicFont to render text that mixes CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) characters with brackets (both full-width `（）` and half-width `()`), Godot generates excessive DrawCalls even with a small number of labels.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a project with a CJK font (e.g., simsun.ttc)
2. Create a LoopContainer or VBoxContainer
3. Add 10-20 labels with text like: `"物品名称（带括号）"` or `"Item (with brackets)"`
4. Observe DrawCalls in the debugger (can reach 100-200+ DrawCalls)

## Expected Behavior

DrawCalls should remain low regardless of whether brackets are mixed with CJK characters.

## Actual Behavior

DrawCalls explode when CJK characters and brackets are mixed:
- 10 labels without brackets: ~20-30 DrawCalls
- 10 labels with CJK + brackets: ~100-200 DrawCalls

## Root Cause Analysis

Godot's DynamicFont uses a font atlas for rendering glyphs. When the atlas page is full, it creates a new page, and each page requires additional DrawCalls. The issue is that:

1. CJK characters are rendered to one atlas page
2. Brackets (both full-width and half-width) are rendered to a different atlas page
3. Each text switch between these pages triggers additional DrawCalls

## Workaround (Current)

```gdscript
# Preload characters by rendering all needed characters at startup
func preload_chars():
    var vp = SubViewport.new()
    vp.size = Vector2i(2048, 512)
    add_child(vp)
    
    var label = Label.new()
    label.add_theme_font_override("font", font)
    label.text = "所有需要预加载的字符（括号）()"  # Include both CJK and brackets
    vp.add_child(label)
    
    await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
    await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
    vp.queue_free()
```

## Suggested Solution

1. Add a `FontFile.preload_chars(chars: String, size: int)` method to preload specific characters to the font atlas at runtime

2. Add a `FontFile.page_size` property that can be set at runtime (currently read-only after loading)

3. Document the font atlas pagination behavior and provide best practices for CJK text rendering

## Environment

- Godot version: 4.6.x
- Renderer: Forward+
- Platform: Windows/Linux/macOS
- Font: DynamicFont with .ttc/.ttf file

## Tags

`rendering` `font` `dynamicfont` `drawcalls` `performance` `cjk`

items.body:
### Tested versions

Godot 4.5 / Godot 4.6 (Testing branches)

### System information

OS: Windows 11 / Windows 10 Mouse: MCHOSE L7 PRO (Running at 4000Hz / 8000Hz polling rate via official driver)

### Issue description

When using a high polling rate mouse (4000Hz or 8000Hz), moving the mouse quickly causes massive CPU spikes and severe frame drops, sometimes completely freezing the main thread.

I initially encountered this while developing my 2D game BOP&POP, where GUI node traversal was suspected. However, the exact same issue persists even in a completely empty project.

Important Note: I have already tried all standard workarounds, but none resolved the underlying stutter:

Input.use_accumulated_input = true is enabled.

Agile Event Flushing is disabled in Project Settings.

physics_object_picking is set to false.

V-Sync is disabled and FPS is capped to monitor refresh rate.

Even setting Input.set_deferred("mouse_mode", Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED) or explicitly calling get_viewport().set_input_as_handled() in _input() to manually throttle the events does not fix it.

It appears the bottleneck is entirely at the OS message pump level (WM_INPUT/Message Queue) or DisplayServer before it even reaches the GDScript input callbacks. The engine struggles to handle the sheer volume of hardware interrupts from modern 8K mice.

Steps to reproduce:

Set the physical mouse polling rate to 4000Hz or 8000Hz via its driver software.

Open the attached empty minimal reproduction project.

Run the project and move the mouse rapidly across the screen.

Observe the severe FPS drop and frame time spikes in the profiler.
